speech.text: Huskies ignore their owner's commands because they're dumb, right? Actually, it's the exact opposite. If you force most mammals to run long distances, they crash as soon as their sugar reserves run out. But huskies are different. Their bodies turn fat into energy so fast, they barely even get tired, making them absolutely perfect for pulling sleds for days on end. They've done this for thousands of years, and that job completely rewired how they think. Most dog breeds were selected to do exactly what humans tell them. Sled dogs are the exact opposite. There's always a lead dog at the front, making split second life or death decisions. If there's thin ice, open water, or a cliff the human can't see, that dog has to ignore the command and steer the team away. For this job, a perfectly obedient dog is actually the most dangerous one. But today, most huskies aren't pulling sleds or making survival choices anymore. The problem is, their brains don't know that. Tell them to sit, and they'll actually weigh the options on whether they feel like it. If they don't like something, they'll happily argue right back at you with all kinds of weird noises.
